learningObjectives.title: 4.5 The seven Ps of the marketing mix

questions.q: A market-oriented business designs its products mainly around:
questions.explain: Market orientation responds to customer needs; product orientation focuses on the product itself.

questions.q: Market share is a firm's sales as a proportion of:
questions.explain: Market share (%) = firm's sales / total market sales × 100.

questions.q: In marketing, STP stands for segmentation, targeting and:
questions.explain: STP: segment the market, target chosen segments, position the product in customers' minds.

questions.q: A niche market is:
questions.explain: Niche marketing targets a small specialised segment; mass marketing targets the whole market.

questions.q: A USP is a product's:
questions.explain: A USP is the feature that differentiates a product from competitors.

questions.q: Dividing a market by age, gender and income is:
questions.explain: Demographic segmentation groups customers by characteristics like age, gender and income.

questions.q: Sales forecasting often uses moving averages to:
options: Smooth data and identify the underlying trend
questions.explain: Moving averages smooth fluctuations in time-series data to reveal trends.

questions.q: A key limitation of forecasting by extrapolation is that it assumes:
questions.explain: Extrapolation projects past trends forward and can be wrong if conditions change.

questions.q: Primary market research is:
options: Data collected first-hand for a specific purpose
questions.explain: Primary research (e.g. surveys) is gathered first-hand; secondary uses existing data.

questions.q: Secondary market research uses:
questions.explain: Secondary research uses already-published data (e.g. reports, government statistics).

questions.q: Qualitative research mainly gathers:
questions.explain: Qualitative research explores opinions/attitudes; quantitative gathers numerical data.

questions.q: A focus group is an example of:
questions.explain: Focus groups collect first-hand qualitative data through guided discussion.

questions.q: The seven Ps are product, price, place, promotion, people, process and:
questions.explain: The extended marketing mix adds people, process and physical evidence to the original 4Ps.

questions.q: Penetration pricing sets a:
options: Low initial price to gain market share
High initial price to maximise early profit
questions.explain: Penetration pricing uses a low price to win share quickly; skimming uses a high initial price.

questions.q: Price skimming typically sets a:
options: High initial price, often for new technology
questions.explain: Skimming charges early adopters a high price, then lowers it over time.

questions.q: The product life cycle stages are introduction, growth, maturity and:
questions.explain: The product life cycle runs introduction → growth → maturity → decline.

questions.q: In the Boston (BCG) matrix, a product with high market share in a high-growth market is a:
questions.explain: Stars have high share in high-growth markets; cash cows have high share in low-growth markets.

questions.q: Cost-plus pricing sets price by adding a:
questions.explain: Cost-plus (mark-up) pricing adds a percentage margin to unit cost.

questions.q: A key challenge of international marketing is:
options: Cultural and language differences between markets
That there are never any customers abroad
That prices must be identical everywhere
questions.explain: International marketing must adapt to cultural, legal and language differences.

questions.q: Modifying a product to suit local tastes in a foreign market is called:
questions.explain: Adaptation tailors the product/marketing to local markets, versus a standardised global approach.

specSource: IB Diploma Business Management guide (first assessment 2024); Unit 4 — Marketing
